subject: Regression of trait on autoregressive parameter

messages.author: 08ad1dfd929670d3
messages.subject: Regression of trait on autoregressive parameter
parts:
Hi all,

 I am interested in the influence of a trait (tsc; trait self-control) on the stability of a repeatedly measured variable in a random-intercept autoregressive model (i.e., the orange arrows):

 

The original syntax (without the orange paths) is:

auto_ep <- "
# random effects
ri =~ 1* ep_t2 + 1* ep_t3 + 1* ep_t4
ri ~~ vari *ri + delta *ep_t1
# mean structure
ep_t1 ~ alpha0 *1
ep_t2 ~ alpha *1 + rho *ep_t1
ep_t3 ~ alpha *1 + rho *ep_t2
ep_t4 ~ alpha *1 + rho *ep_t3
# residual coepriance model
ep_t1 ~~ resepr0 *ep_t1
ep_t2 ~~ resepr *ep_t2
ep_t3 ~~ resepr *ep_t3
ep_t4 ~~ resepr *ep_t4
ri ~ tsc rs ~ tsc"

It seems easy to regress tsc on eta ("ri") by adding "ri ~ tsc".

But, adding a regression on the autoregressive parameter ("rho", by "rho ~ tsc") results in the error message: “lavaan ERROR: missing observed variables in dataset: rho”.

Well, it seems problematic to regress a trait on an individual parameter. However, I am interested in the effect of tsc on the stability coefficient, expecting high tsc being associated with more stability.

 

Do you know how to add a regression on an autoregressive parameter in the syntax?

 Best regards,

Korbi

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Regression of trait on autoregressive parameter
parts:
On 12/16/22 12:00, Korbi wrote:
> However, I am interested in the effect of tsc on the
> stability coefficient, expecting high tsc being associated with more
> stability.

You cannot have a model parameter (rho) as the outcome of a regression.
What you describe sounds like 'moderation', which is equivalent to
adding interaction terms. For example for Y2, you could have

Y2 ~ a*Y1
Y2 ~ b*tsc
Y2 ~ c*Y1.tsc

where I would create Y1.tsc as the product term of Y1 and tsc in the
data.frame. You could do the same for Y3 and Y4 and set appropriate
equality constraints.

Yves.
